Proven on a two-participant fixture registry (test_two_counterparties_on_different_releases_are_read_differently): the same bytes decode from the participant that has cut over and are refused from the one that has not. WHAT IS STILL MISSING: this build understands exactly ONE wire dialect -- REQUEST_WIRE_FIELDS/RESPONSE_WIRE_FIELDS are version-blind, so the table can currently only express WHICH participants are on v1, never run a genuine v1/v2 pair. A release weekend cannot be rehearsed until the field sets are keyed by version, which is the remaining build item for this question.

company/interfaces/wall_protocol.py:176-179 -- a version outside SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS raises UNSUPPORTED_VERSION and an absent one raises MISSING_FIELD, so the stamp is ENFORCED on receipt rather than carried. What was built: every message on the payment observable seam now travels inside a transport frame stating its participant (simulation/payment_seam_adapter.py::frame_wire_message, PARTICIPANT_ID='BACS-BUREAU-01'), and company/interfaces/wall_protocol.py::decode_framed_response refuses an unregistered sender (UNKNOWN_SENDER), a wrong credential (BAD_CREDENTIAL) and a release that counterparty is not on (VERSION_NOT_SPOKEN) BEFORE the envelope is read. It is below the port in the reviewer's sense: company/billing/payment_observation_consumer.py::observe_wire, the live triad's only route to a payment observation, cannot reach belief code without passing it. NOT A TAUTOLOGY: the company holds a sha256 FINGERPRINT and the credential itself lives only in the counterparty's module -- test_MUTATION_a_rotated_credential_the_company_was_not_told_about_BREAKS_the_seam rotates it and the live crossing stops working. WHAT IS NOT DONE, and is why the verdict does not move: (1) two of three crossings are still unframed (company/comms/susceptibility_estimator.py, company/market/flex_participation.py) -- named in _UNFRAMED_CROSSINGS and held by a ratchet test so a fourth cannot join them silently; (2) no cryptography -- no certificate chain and no signature over the bytes, so what is modelled is the REFUSAL and not SMKI/DIP signing itself. A real network would not accept a credential presented in the clear.

Nothing stops a stand-in configuration reaching production because nothing distinguishes them: no environment segregation and no startup assertion exists across interface/contracts/, company/interfaces/, simulation/payment_seam_adapter.py or sim/flex_dispatch.py. The network-isolation wall makes the question moot TODAY (the company has no route out at all), but the reviewer's subject is the go-live seam, which is what this atom claims to be.

Nothing runs against DCC SIT/UIT/UEPT, CSS test or the DIP test environments -- a repo-wide search finds no such target -- and this layer feeds no Elexon qualification or REC entry-assessment evidence. Same wall as Q9: reaching those systems means contacting real organisations and spending real money (reserved classes 1 and 2). EP19_counterparty_qualification_paths (epoch 5) is where that register lives.
